claude_proposed_widenings.name: create_space family (pocket_dimension / spatial_pocket)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Rope Trick creates a persistent extradimensional space that creatures can voluntarily enter and inhabit for the spell's duration. This requires a payload family that models: (1) an object/location attachment (the rope + portal at its tip), (2) a capacity constraint (up to 8 Medium creatures), (3) blocking effects preventing pass-through of attacks/spells/effects, (4) automatic ejection on spell end (fall_on_end). No existing payload family can model this — ongoing_effect's OngoingOperation is constrained to roll_modifier and damage_on_hit; activation only has attack_roll and save_gate phases.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: an invisible 3-foot-by-5-foot portal opens to an extradimensional space that lasts until the spell ends... Attacks, spells, and other effects can't pass into or out of the space

claude_proposed_widenings.name: object attachment in Attachment union (types.ts)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rope is the attachment target (casting time: Touch, caster touches a rope). The v4 taxonomy includes 'object' as an attachment atom, but it is absent from the types.ts Attachment union. Rope Trick must attach to the rope as an object to model the portal correctly.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You touch a rope. One end of it hovers upward...

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Spell Effect variants: block_targeting, block_travel, transport_exile, fall_on_end
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell's persistent effects require: (1) blocking all attacks/spells/effects from passing through the portal boundary (block_targeting + block_travel), (2) transporting entering creatures into the extradimensional space (transport_exile), (3) ejecting all contents when the spell ends (fall_on_end). All four atoms exist in v4 taxonomy but are absent from the spell Effect union (DamageEffect | NoneEffect). Even if a family existed, these effects could not be expressed.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Attacks, spells, and other effects can't pass into or out of the space... Anything inside the space drops out when the spell ends.
